_readme: Internship, traineeship and master’s-thesis programmes from OFFICIAL sources only (EU institutions, international organisations, research centres, universities, governments). Never invent dates or amounts — use null and a note. statusOverride: null (computed from opens/deadline), "varies" (rolling/per-vacancy), "unconfirmed" (next cycle not announced), "closed". Checked weekly — see AGENT.md.

programmes.title: European Commission Blue Book Traineeship
programmes.summary: Five-month paid traineeships in the European Commission and other EU bodies, mainly in Brussels and Luxembourg, run twice a year.
programmes.location: Brussels, Luxembourg and other Commission sites
eligibility: A completed university degree of at least three years (EQF level 6) by the application deadline.
EU nationals: English, French or German at C1/C2 (or mother tongue) plus a second EU language at B2.
Non-EU nationals: English, French or German at C1/C2 (or mother tongue).
Not more than six weeks of previous work or traineeship in an EU institution.
programmes.nationalities: Nationals of EU member states, and a limited number of places for nationals of candidate countries with a pre-accession strategy.
programmes.stipend: Paid traineeship (monthly grant set by the Commission — see the official site).

dates.deadlineNote: Applications for the October 2027 session (1 Oct 2027 – 29 Feb 2028) run 15 Feb – 12 Mar 2027, closing 10:00 Brussels time. The March 2027 session application closed on 4 Sep 2026.

procedure: Choose a strand (administrative or translation).
Apply online on the Blue Book portal during the application period.
Pre-selected candidates are entered in the Virtual Blue Book, from which services choose trainees.

verification.notes: Session dates and eligibility from the Blue Book website.

warnings: Most places are for EU nationals; Pakistan is not an EU candidate country.

programmes.title: European Parliament Schuman Traineeships
programmes.summary: Paid five-month traineeships at the European Parliament in Brussels, Luxembourg, Strasbourg or its liaison offices, in policy, law, communication, finance, IT and more.
programmes.location: Brussels, Luxembourg, Strasbourg or a liaison office
eligibility: A university degree of at least EQF level 6 (or, for limited places, an EU vocational qualification of at least two years).
You may apply before getting your diploma but must confirm it at least three months before the start.
At least 18 years old.
programmes.nationalities: Mainly EU nationals; the Parliament can offer a very limited number of traineeships to non-EU applicants.
programmes.stipend: Paid (monthly grant published by the Parliament each year).
programmes.duration: About 5 months (1 Mar – 31 Jul or 1 Oct – end Feb)

dates.deadlineNote: Apply 1–31 May for traineeships starting 1 October; apply 1–31 October for traineeships starting 1 March.

procedure: Apply online on the Parliament’s traineeship application site during the window.
Non-EU trainees arrange their own visa and permits (not reimbursed).

verification.notes: Windows and eligibility from the official FAQ; the grant amount is in a separate yearly PDF.

programmes.title: JRC Scientific Traineeships (European Commission)
programmes.summary: Scientific traineeships of up to five months at the Commission’s research centre sites (Ispra, Seville, Karlsruhe, Petten, Geel, Brussels) for recent graduates and current master’s or PhD students.
programmes.location: JRC sites: Ispra (Italy), Seville (Spain), Karlsruhe (Germany), Petten (Netherlands), Geel and Brussels (Belgium)
eligibility: At least a three-year bachelor’s degree, and either graduated in the last five years or currently enrolled in a master’s or PhD.
Very good knowledge of the language(s) set in the call.
Not more than six weeks of previous work or traineeship in an EU institution.
programmes.nationalities: Normally nationals of EU member states, candidate countries and countries associated to the EU research programme; others only by derogation.
programmes.stipend: Monthly allowance of 25% of the basic pay of an AD5 step 1 official, adjusted for the site.

dates.deadlineNote: Each call sets its own topics and deadline — see the JRC Recruitment Portal.

procedure: Find an open call on the JRC Recruitment Portal.
Apply online before the call deadline.

sources.label: JRC — Rules governing the scientific traineeship programme (V12, 2025)

verification.notes: Eligibility and allowance from the official JRC rules (2025).

programmes.title: European Central Bank Traineeships
programmes.summary: Paid traineeships of 3–6 months at the ECB in Frankfurt for students and recent graduates in economics, finance, law, IT and more.
programmes.fields: Economics, finance, law, IT and more
eligibility: At least a bachelor’s degree.
Fluent English and one other EU official language.
Current students (including PhD) and recent graduates with at most 12 months’ professional experience since qualifying.
Not previously an ECB trainee or employee.
programmes.nationalities: Nationals of EU member states or acceding countries.
programmes.stipend: €1,170 a month (€2,120 for PhD traineeships); accommodation paid if you relocate more than 50 km.

dates.deadlineNote: Each traineeship vacancy has its own closing date.

procedure: Apply to a specific traineeship vacancy on the ECB careers site.
Selection starts on the closing date and usually takes about three months.

verification.notes: From the ECB traineeship page.

programmes.title: CERN Summer Student Programme
programmes.summary: Summer research placements of 8–13 weeks at CERN for bachelor’s and master’s students in physics, computing, engineering or mathematics.
eligibility: Bachelor’s or master’s student in physics, computing, engineering or mathematics.
Students from Canada, Japan and the United States apply through their national programmes.
programmes.nationalities: All nationalities are welcome to apply (except Canada, Japan, USA — national routes).
programmes.stipend: Not stated on the programme page — see careers.cern/summer.

dates.deadlineNote: CERN says applications must arrive no later than the end of January; check careers.cern/summer for the 2027 deadline.

procedure: Complete the application form on careers.cern/summer.

verification.notes: Eligibility and duration from home.cern; 2027 deadline and allowance to be confirmed on careers.cern.

programmes.title: CERN Technical Studentship (internship or master’s thesis)
programmes.summary: Technical studentships let bachelor’s and master’s students spend a placement at CERN, including for a final-year project or thesis, in engineering, IT, applied physics and related fields.
eligibility: Enrolled bachelor’s or master’s student in a relevant technical field (see each studentship call).
programmes.nationalities: Nationals of CERN member and associate member states. CERN currently cannot consider applications from nationals of Pakistan, Lithuania, Cyprus, Latvia, Croatia and Türkiye (quota reached).
programmes.stipend: Monthly allowance — see the studentship call.

dates.deadlineNote: CERN publishes technical studentship calls with selection rounds on careers.cern.

procedure: Check eligibility on careers.cern.
Apply to the technical studentship call that matches your field.

verification.notes: Nationality rules from careers.cern; call details must be read on each call page.

warnings: Pakistani nationals currently cannot apply (CERN quota reached).

programmes.title: ESA Graduate Trainee Programme
programmes.summary: One-year paid traineeships (possible second year) at ESA establishments for recent master’s graduates in engineering, science, IT or business services.
programmes.location: ESA sites in the Netherlands, Germany, Italy, Spain, France and elsewhere
eligibility: A master’s degree in engineering, science, IT or business services, within one year of graduation (final-year students must graduate before the start).
programmes.nationalities: Citizens of ESA member states, associate members, European Cooperating States, or Canada.
programmes.stipend: Monthly salary (exempt from national income tax), plus installation allowance and travel.

dates.deadlineNote: Opportunities are usually published in February on jobs.esa.int, with interviews March–May and start in September–October.

procedure: Find graduate trainee opportunities on jobs.esa.int (usually February).
Apply to up to three positions with CV and motivation letter.

verification.notes: From ESA’s programme page.

warnings: Only for nationals of ESA member/associate/cooperating states.

programmes.title: DAAD RISE Germany — research internships
programmes.summary: Summer research internships of about three months in German university and research labs, mentored by PhD students, for undergraduates from North America, the UK and Ireland.
programmes.location: Universities and research institutes across Germany
eligibility: Enrolled in a bachelor’s programme at a university in the US, Canada, the UK or Ireland (international students: studied there for more than 12 months by the deadline).
Biology, chemistry, computer science, physics, earth sciences, engineering or related fields.
At least two years of the degree completed by the start, and still an undergraduate afterwards.
programmes.nationalities: Any nationality, if enrolled at an eligible university in the US, Canada, the UK or Ireland.
programmes.stipend: €992 a month DAAD scholarship (US, UK, Irish students) plus insurance and travel subsidy; Canadian students via Mitacs receive CAD 7,000.
programmes.duration: About 3 months (10 weeks – 90 days), starting 15 May – 15 July 2027

dates.deadlineNote: Applications in the RISE database 15 Oct – 30 Nov 2026 (11:59 pm CET); references by 15 Dec 2026; placements announced Feb/Mar 2027.

procedure: Register for a DAAD ID and open the RISE Germany internship database.
Apply to projects with a motivation letter per project, CV, course list, transcript and enrolment certificate.
A PhD-holding academic submits a reference online by 15 December.

sources.label: DAAD RISE Germany — What applicants need to know

verification.notes: All facts from the DAAD RISE page for summer 2027.

warnings: Only for students enrolled in the US, Canada, the UK or Ireland.

programmes.title: ETH Zurich Student Summer Research Fellowship (Computer Science)
programmes.provider: ETH Zurich, Department of Computer Science
programmes.summary: Two-month paid summer research fellowships in ETH Zurich computer science groups for bachelor’s and master’s students from any university.
eligibility: Enrolled in a bachelor’s or master’s programme in computer science or a closely related field (electrical engineering, mathematics, physics).
Graduating in 2028 or later; at least two years of study completed by July 2027.
Good working knowledge of English.
programmes.nationalities: Any nationality.
programmes.stipend: CHF 4,000 for housing and living costs, plus travel and visa expenses.

dates.deadlineNote: Apply 1 Nov – 16 Dec 2026, closing 13:00 CET; decisions by end of February 2027.

procedure: Register on SiROP (sirop.org) and open the fellowship’s opportunity page.
Upload an English Europass CV, official transcript and one-page motivation letter.
Choose one or two research areas that match your background.

sources.label: ETH Zurich — Summer Research Fellowship: How to apply

verification.notes: Dates, eligibility and stipend from the ETH page.

programmes.title: EPFL Excellence Research Internship Program
programmes.summary: Research internships of about three months in EPFL labs for top bachelor’s and master’s students nominated by partner universities in North America and Singapore.
eligibility: Enrolled at a partner university in North America or Singapore (others can ask ERIP to check eligibility).
Top 10% of your class; at least two years of a bachelor’s completed.
Nominated by your home university’s international office.
programmes.nationalities: Depends on the partner university, not nationality.
programmes.stipend: Excellence scholarship for up to three months (amount not stated on the page).

dates.deadlineNote: Applications close 30 Nov 2026; references by 6 Dec; shortlist by end of December.

procedure: Get nominated by your home university.
Apply online with CV, motivation letter, transcripts, two referees, passport scan and three EPFL lab choices.

sources.label: EPFL — Research internships: eligibility and application

verification.notes: From the EPFL page.

warnings: Only for students of EPFL partner universities in North America and Singapore.

programmes.title: Mitacs Globalink Research Internship (Canada)
programmes.summary: 12-week funded summer research internships at Canadian universities for senior undergraduates from Mitacs partner countries.
eligibility: Full-time undergraduate (or combined undergraduate/master’s) student, 18 or older, with 1–3 semesters left in fall 2027.
Minimum grades set per country; graduate students are not eligible.
programmes.nationalities: Citizens/students of Mitacs partner countries, including Austria, Brazil, Chile, China, Colombia, Finland, France, Germany, Hong Kong, India, Ireland, Jordan, Mexico, Pakistan, Peru, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand, Tunisia, Ukraine, the UK and the US (some through a partner organisation).
programmes.stipend: Contribution to airfare, housing, food and incidentals stipends, enrolment fees and health insurance (amounts vary by country).

dates.deadlineNote: The Summer 2027 student call has closed. Mitacs usually opens student applications in June for about six weeks.

procedure: Check your country’s eligibility and any partner pre-steps.
Apply on the Globalink student platform to 3–10 projects in at least three provinces during the June window.

verification.notes: Eligibility, funding and timeline from the Mitacs page; country list changes each year.

programmes.title: OIST Research Internship (Japan)
programmes.provider: Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology (OIST)
programmes.summary: Funded 4–6 month research internships in OIST labs in Okinawa for final-year bachelor’s students, master’s students and graduates.
eligibility: In the last two years of a bachelor’s, any year of a master’s, or already holding one of these degrees.
Current or graduated PhD students are not eligible.
Enrolled students need approval from their home institution.
programmes.nationalities: Any nationality.
programmes.stipend: 2,400 JPY per working day, round-trip flight and furnished housing.

dates.deadlineNote: Fall 2027 round (Oct 2027 – Mar 2028): deadline 15 April 2027, 23:59 JST. The Spring 2027 round closed on 15 Oct 2026. Schedule marked tentative by OIST. Application fee 5,000 JPY.

procedure: Find an available lab on OIST’s faculty availability page.
Apply online with transcripts, a 250-word statement, CV, 1–3 professor recommendation letters and ID.
Pay the 5,000 JPY application fee.

verification.notes: From OIST’s programme and application pages.

programmes.title: KAUST Visiting Student Research Program (VSRP)
programmes.provider: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology
programmes.summary: Fully funded 2–6 month research internships in KAUST labs for third-year-and-above undergraduates and master’s students in STEM, with start dates any time of year.
eligibility: Undergraduate in 3rd year or above, or master’s student, in a STEM field.
Minimum GPA 3.5/4 (or equivalent) and English proficiency.
Current PhD candidates and KAUST students/alumni are not eligible.
programmes.nationalities: Any nationality.
programmes.stipend: USD 1,000 a month, private room and bathroom, and return airfare.

dates.deadlineNote: Applications are accepted all year round; one application at a time; no fee.

procedure: Choose a project on the KAUST internship search page and click Apply.
Submit transcripts, passport, statement of purpose, CV and one faculty recommendation.

verification.notes: From the KAUST internships page.

programmes.title: World Bank Group Internship (Bank Internship Program)
programmes.summary: Paid internships at the World Bank Group, mainly in Washington, D.C., for final-year undergraduates and master’s/PhD students.
eligibility: Final-year undergraduate, or currently pursuing a master’s or PhD.
Fluent English; 0–6 years of work experience.
programmes.nationalities: Citizens of World Bank Group member countries.
programmes.stipend: Competitive hourly salary.

dates.deadlineNote: Spring/summer cycle applications usually run January–February; winter/fall cycle July–August. Exact 2027 dates are published on the careers site.

procedure: Prepare a CV (max 2 pages), cover letter (max 1 page) and proof of enrolment.
Apply on the World Bank Group careers site to up to three positions.

verification.notes: From the World Bank internship page.

programmes.title: IMF Fund Internship Program (FIP)
programmes.summary: Paid 10–12 week summer internships at IMF headquarters in Washington, D.C.; about 50 interns a year are recruited worldwide.
eligibility: See the IMF vacancy notice for degree requirements.
programmes.nationalities: Recruitment is global (see the vacancy notice).
programmes.stipend: Paid (amount not stated on the programme page).

dates.deadlineNote: Applications typically open in early December on the IMF Career Site.

procedure: Watch the IMF Career Site from early December and apply to the Fund Internship Program vacancy.

verification.notes: Duration and timing from the IMF page; eligibility is in the yearly vacancy notice.

programmes.title: WHO Internship Programme
programmes.summary: Full-time internships of 6–24 weeks at WHO headquarters in Geneva and in regional and country offices, in public health, medicine, management, communications and more.
eligibility: At least 20 years old.
Enrolled in a relevant programme (after at least three years of full-time study) or graduated within the last 18 months.
Fluent in a working language of the office.
programmes.nationalities: Passport holders of a WHO member state.
programmes.stipend: Living allowance for eligible selected interns who need financial support (amount in each vacancy); medical and accident insurance covered.

dates.deadlineNote: Internships are posted continuously, each with its own deadline.

procedure: Apply only through internship vacancies on the WHO careers site (Stellis).

verification.notes: From the WHO internship page.

programmes.title: UNESCO Internship Programme
programmes.summary: Unpaid internships of 1–6 months at UNESCO headquarters in Paris and field offices; you join a talent pool valid for six months.
eligibility: At least 20 years old.
Final or third year of a bachelor’s, enrolled in a master’s/PhD, or graduated in the last 12 months.
Excellent English or French.
programmes.nationalities: Not restricted on the programme page.
programmes.stipend: Unpaid — UNESCO does not remunerate interns.

dates.deadlineNote: You apply to a talent pool at any time; applications stay valid for six months.

procedure: Apply through “Apply Now” on the UNESCO Careers internship page with CV and motivation letter (English or French).

verification.notes: From the UNESCO internship page.

warnings: Unpaid — you must cover travel and living costs.

programmes.title: IAEA Internship Programme
programmes.summary: Internships at the IAEA in Vienna; full-time interns receive a monthly stipend.
eligibility: See the IAEA internship pages and each opportunity for requirements.
programmes.nationalities: See the IAEA internship pages.
programmes.stipend: €1,000 a month for full-time interns (living-cost allowance).

dates.deadlineNote: Internship opportunities are published on the IAEA employment site.

procedure: Apply to internship opportunities through the IAEA employment site.

verification.notes: Stipend from the IAEA conditions page; eligibility to be read on the IAEA internship pages.

programmes.title: Erasmus+ Traineeships for Students
programmes.summary: Erasmus+ funds traineeships of 2–12 months with an organisation anywhere in the world for students (and recent graduates) of universities in Erasmus+ programme countries.
eligibility: Enrolled at a university in an Erasmus+ programme country holding the Erasmus Charter (short-cycle, bachelor’s, master’s or doctoral level); also open to recent graduates.
programmes.nationalities: Depends on your university, not nationality — e.g. international students at an Italian university can take part.
programmes.stipend: Erasmus+ grant through your university (rates in the Erasmus+ Programme Guide).

dates.deadlineNote: Each university’s Erasmus/international office sets its own call and deadlines.

procedure: Contact your university’s Erasmus+ or international office.
Find a host organisation and agree a training plan, then apply in your university’s call.

verification.notes: From the Erasmus+ page.

programmes.title: Fraunhofer — master’s theses, internships and student jobs
programmes.summary: Fraunhofer’s 70+ applied-research institutes in Germany offer bachelor’s and master’s theses, internships and paid student assistant jobs, posted on one job portal.
programmes.fields: Engineering, IT, natural sciences, applied research
eligibility: Currently enrolled at a higher education institution.
Each position lists its own requirements (often German or English).
programmes.nationalities: Not restricted on the student page — check each position.
programmes.stipend: Depends on the position (student assistant jobs are paid).

dates.deadlineNote: Positions are posted continuously on the Fraunhofer job portal; apply to each one separately.

procedure: Search jobs.fraunhofer.de with the thesis or internship filter.
Apply to each position separately.

verification.notes: From the Fraunhofer student page.

warnings: Only for PhD students at A*STAR partner universities — students cannot apply on their own.
programmes.title: A*STAR Research Attachment Programme (ARAP)
programmes.provider: Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR)
programmes.summary: PhD students from A*STAR’s overseas partner universities spend 1–2 years of their doctorate doing research in an A*STAR institute in Singapore, with a monthly stipend and allowances.
eligibility: PhD students (or applicants with proof of acceptance into a PhD) at an A*STAR partner university; integrated MSc-PhD students only during the PhD phase.
Bachelor’s degree with at least Second Class (Upper) Honours or equivalent, strong references and research track record.
Jointly nominated by the home university and an A*STAR supervisor.
programmes.nationalities: Not restricted by nationality on the official page — eligibility depends on being at a partner university.
programmes.stipend: S$3,600 a month, S$300 a month housing allowance, S$1,500 airfare grant, S$1,000 settling-in and S$800 IT allowance; visa, medical insurance and a conference allowance are also covered. Tuition fees are not covered.

dates.deadlineNote: A*STAR researchers submit nominations by 1 June or 1 December each year; the start date must be at least 6 months after the nomination deadline.

procedure: Check whether your university is an A*STAR partner and contact its international or doctoral office.
Agree a joint project with an A*STAR supervisor.
The A*STAR researcher submits the nomination by 1 June or 1 December.

verification.notes: From the A*STAR ARAP page.

warnings: Only for PhD students at RIKEN partner universities, with a RIKEN host researcher.
programmes.title: RIKEN International Program Associate (IPA)
programmes.summary: Non-Japanese doctoral students at RIKEN’s partner universities carry out their PhD research at a RIKEN laboratory in Japan for 1–3 years, with a daily living allowance and housing.
programmes.fields: Natural sciences, engineering, computing and life sciences
eligibility: Enrolled in a PhD programme at a Japanese or overseas partner university of RIKEN (partners include universities in Pakistan, China, India, Malaysia, Germany, the UK and others — see the list).
A RIKEN researcher must agree to host you.
programmes.nationalities: Non-Japanese doctoral candidates.
programmes.stipend: 5,200 JPY a day living allowance; free on-campus housing or off-campus rent up to 70,000 JPY a month; one round-trip airfare and accident insurance.

dates.cycle: Calls in April and September each year
dates.deadlineNote: Calls for overseas applicants are issued in April and September each year; start in October–April or April–October. Exact dates are in each call.

procedure: Check that your university and department are on RIKEN’s IPA partner list.
Contact the RIKEN researcher you want to work with; they contact RIKEN’s Research Personnel Affairs Section.
Apply during the April or September call following its instructions.

verification.notes: From the RIKEN IPA page.

programmes.title: Council of the EU — Consilium traineeship
programmes.provider: General Secretariat of the Council of the European Union
programmes.summary: Five-month paid traineeships in Brussels in policy, law, administration, communications, translation and IT, twice a year (110 places a year).
programmes.fields: Policy, law, administration, communications, translation, IT
eligibility: EU citizenship.
A bachelor’s degree or higher.
Very good English or French and at least one other EU language.
No previous work experience at another EU institution.
programmes.nationalities: EU citizens only.
programmes.stipend: Paid traineeship with allowances and other benefits (amount set in the Council’s traineeship rules — not stated on the main page).
programmes.duration: 5 months (1 Feb–30 Jun or 1 Sep–31 Jan)

dates.deadlineNote: Applications open on 8 February 2027 (application period in February and March). The exact closing date is published when the call opens.

procedure: Read the Council’s application procedure before the period opens.
Apply online during the February–March period.
Selection takes place from April to June.

sources.label: Council of the EU — Consilium traineeships

verification.notes: From the Council traineeships page (last reviewed 18 Sep 2026).

warnings: Online-only or non-degree programmes are not accepted.
programmes.title: OECD Internship Programme
programmes.provider: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
programmes.summary: Internships of one to six months supporting OECD policy analysts or corporate teams, mostly at the Paris headquarters, with applications accepted all year.
programmes.location: OECD headquarters, Paris, France (in person, hybrid or remote)
programmes.fields: Economics, policy, data, environment, education, health, law, IT, communications and more
eligibility: Enrolled in a full-time accredited degree programme (bachelor’s, master’s or PhD) for the whole internship.
Excellent English or French and working knowledge of (or willingness to learn) the other.
Good quantitative, IT and drafting skills; available for at least one month.
programmes.nationalities: Primarily OECD member-country nationals; also open to non-member nationals for specific programmes and projects.
programmes.stipend: €1,000 per full month for interns located in Paris, plus 2.5 days’ leave a month.
programmes.duration: 1 to 6 months (renewable up to 12), full time

dates.deadlineNote: Applications accepted all year; selection can take up to three months, so apply well before your availability.

procedure: Use the OECD eligibility tester.
Apply on the OECD’s SmartRecruiters platform with your cover letter in “Message to Hiring Manager”.
Shortlisted candidates may be interviewed or tested.

verification.notes: From the OECD internships page.

warnings: Unpaid — you need your own funding for living costs in the duty station.
programmes.title: United Nations Secretariat Internship Programme
programmes.summary: Two- to six-month internships in UN Secretariat departments and offices — for example in New York, Geneva, Vienna or Bangkok — advertised as individual openings on the UN Careers portal.
programmes.location: UN Secretariat duty stations (filter by duty station on UN Careers)
programmes.fields: Political affairs, economics, communications, law, IT, administration and more
eligibility: Final year of a bachelor’s programme, enrolled in a master’s or PhD, or within one year after graduation.
Excellent English or French.
Not a child or sibling of a UN Secretariat staff member.
programmes.nationalities: No nationality restriction stated.
programmes.stipend: Unpaid — the UN does not pay interns; you or your sponsor cover travel, insurance, housing and living costs.

dates.deadlineNote: Each internship is advertised separately on UN Careers with its own deadline.

procedure: Search “internship” on careers.un.org and filter by duty station.
Read the job opening and apply through the Inspira account you are redirected to.

verification.notes: From the UN internship fact sheet and current UN Careers internship openings.

programmes.title: MBZUAI Global Research Internship Program (MGRIP)
programmes.provider: Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence
programmes.summary: A fully funded four-week AI research residency in Abu Dhabi for undergraduate and master’s students from around the world (formerly UGRIP).
programmes.fields: Artificial intelligence: machine learning, computer vision, NLP, robotics, computational biology, statistics
eligibility: In the penultimate year of a STEM undergraduate or master’s degree, completing it after September 2027.
Minimum CGPA 3.5/4.0 or equivalent.
English: IELTS Academic 6.5, TOEFL iBT 90, PTE 60, Cambridge C1 180 / C2 200 or Duolingo 120 (test-centre exams only; proof required at application).
programmes.nationalities: All nationalities.
programmes.stipend: Fully funded: accommodation, health insurance, visa, airfares, airport transfers and a stipend (amount not stated).

dates.deadlineNote: Applications 1 January – 28 February 2027 (5 p.m. Gulf time); decisions by 2 April 2027.

procedure: Check the 2027 projects (released in November).
Prepare your English test result and documents.
Apply online between 1 January and 28 February 2027.

verification.notes: From the MBZUAI MGRIP page (2027 admission cycle).

programmes.title: Westlake University Summer Research Internship
programmes.summary: A five-week summer research internship in Westlake University laboratories in Hangzhou for international students, with free campus housing and a living allowance.
programmes.fields: Science, engineering, life sciences and related fields
eligibility: Non-Chinese citizens with a valid passport.
Current undergraduate or graduate students, or recent bachelor’s/master’s graduates (2026 call: graduating in 2027 or 2028, or already graduated).
English proficiency evidence and transcripts.
programmes.nationalities: Non-Chinese citizens.
programmes.stipend: 2026 edition: living allowance of 1,760 RMB and free on-campus housing; visa, insurance and travel paid by the intern.
programmes.duration: About 5 weeks in July–August (2026: 13 July – 14 August)

dates.deadlineNote: The 2027 call has not been published yet. The 2026 call closed on 31 March 2026.

procedure: Register on Westlake’s graduate application system and choose a programme.
Upload passport, diplomas, transcripts, English evidence and research outputs.
Supervisors may hold an online interview.

verification.notes: From Westlake’s official 2026 call; 2027 dates not yet announced.

warnings: Requires an official recommendation from an organisation that has an agreement with KIST.
programmes.title: KIST School Internship Program
programmes.provider: Korea Institute of Science and Technology (KIST)
programmes.summary: Six-month paid research internships at KIST in Seoul for students planning to apply to the KIST School (UST) master’s or PhD programme, starting in March or September.
programmes.fields: Science and engineering research at KIST
eligibility: Keep your student status at your current university throughout the internship, with fewer than 3 semesters left until graduation.
Potential applicant to the KIST School (UST) graduate programme.
Official recommendation from an organisation that has an agreement with KIST.
programmes.nationalities: Students recommended through organisations with a KIST agreement.
programmes.stipend: 1,200,000 KRW a month for undergraduates and 1,400,000 KRW for master’s students (before tax); dormitory about 180,000 KRW; insurance included.
programmes.duration: 6 months (spring from March, fall from September)

dates.deadlineNote: Admission guidelines are announced for each intake; deadlines depend on the recommending organisation.

procedure: Find advisors on the KIST School or UST websites.
Ask whether your university or national agency has an agreement with KIST to recommend you.
Submit the application when guidelines are announced; document review, recommendation and interview follow.

verification.notes: From the KIST School internship page.

warnings: Only for master’s students at EU universities outside the Czech Republic.
programmes.title: IOCB Prague Summer Student Program
programmes.provider: Institute of Organic Chemistry and Biochemistry of the Czech Academy of Sciences
programmes.summary: An eight-week summer research placement in Prague for master’s students in chemistry and the life sciences, with a dormitory room and a stipend.
programmes.fields: Organic chemistry, biochemistry, molecular biology, computational or theoretical chemistry
eligibility: Already started a master’s degree in a related field.
At a university in the EU, outside the Czech Republic.
Not already on Erasmus or another fellowship.
programmes.nationalities: Students of EU universities (outside the Czech Republic).
programmes.stipend: Accommodation in a nearby dormitory and a stipend of around €1,000 for the 8 weeks; travel paid by the student.

dates.deadlineNote: Details for 2027 will be announced in early 2027. The 2026 deadline was 26 April.

procedure: Check the participating research groups on the programme page.
Apply online before the deadline announced in early 2027.
Results by the end of May.

verification.notes: From the IOCB Prague programme page.

warnings: Pay is not guaranteed — confirm funding with the group leader before you travel.
programmes.title: EMBL undergraduate research internships
programmes.summary: Research internships for natural-science undergraduates in EMBL research groups, arranged directly with the group leader.
programmes.location: EMBL Heidelberg and other EMBL sites
programmes.fields: Biology, chemistry, physics, computer science, engineering and other natural sciences
eligibility: Undergraduate students in any natural-science discipline.
Contact a group leader directly with CV, interests, purpose, length and timing of the internship, and a referee.
programmes.nationalities: No nationality restriction stated.
programmes.stipend: Payment possible at the group leader’s discretion (from the group’s grants); not guaranteed.

dates.deadlineNote: No fixed deadline — timing is agreed with the group leader.

procedure: Choose groups on EMBL’s research units pages.
Email the group leader with your CV and a short letter.
Arrange dates, funding and accommodation with the group.

verification.notes: From EMBL’s undergraduate internships page.

programmes.title: Aalto Science Institute (AScI) International Summer Research Programme
programmes.summary: A paid 12-week summer research internship in Aalto University research groups in Espoo for bachelor’s and master’s students from anywhere in the world.
programmes.fields: Science, engineering, computer science and related fields (project list published mid-December)
eligibility: Bachelor’s or master’s students worldwide (doctoral students only in exceptional cases).
Choose from the projects listed by Aalto research groups.
programmes.nationalities: Open to students worldwide.
programmes.stipend: Salary of 2,000+ EUR a month depending on years of study, plus a travel bonus of 400 EUR (from inside Europe) or 800 EUR (from outside Europe).

dates.deadlineNote: Applications 7–31 January 2027 (strict deadline 23:59 Finnish time). Projects listed mid-December 2026; interviews in February; decisions in the second week of March.

procedure: Read the project list when it is published in mid-December 2026.
Apply online between 7 and 31 January 2027.
Shortlisted applicants are interviewed in February.

sources.label: Aalto University — AScI International Summer Research Programme

verification.notes: From the Aalto AScI programme page (2027 call).

programmes.title: RCSI StAR Summer Research Internships
programmes.provider: RCSI University of Medicine and Health Sciences
programmes.summary: Eight-week summer research internships in Dublin for undergraduates heading into their final year who plan to do a PhD, with a stipend and free city-centre accommodation.
programmes.fields: Basic science and health sciences research
eligibility: Entering the final year of an undergraduate degree in basic science or health sciences after the internship.
A clear plan to pursue a PhD.
programmes.nationalities: Any nationality; non-EU students need a visa and Irish residence permit (RCSI helps successful applicants).
programmes.stipend: €2,000 stipend and paid accommodation in Dublin city centre; travel not included.

dates.deadlineNote: Applications for this year’s intake are closed; the next call has not been published yet.

procedure: Watch the StAR page for the next call.
Informal questions: StARintern@rcsi.ie.

verification.notes: From the RCSI StAR summer internships page.

programmes.title: IIMCB student internships (Warsaw)
programmes.provider: International Institute of Molecular and Cell Biology in Warsaw
programmes.summary: Paid two-month full-time research internships in IIMCB laboratories in Warsaw for bachelor’s and master’s students or recent graduates, with applications accepted all year.
programmes.fields: Molecular and cell biology, structural biology, bioinformatics
eligibility: Enrolled in a bachelor’s or master’s programme, or recently graduated.
Places are limited; only selected candidates are offered an internship.
programmes.nationalities: No nationality restriction stated (international, English-speaking teams).
programmes.stipend: 2,500 PLN net a month.

dates.deadlineNote: No fixed deadline — applications accepted on a rolling basis.

procedure: Read the research topics of the IIMCB laboratories.
Send your CV and the registration form as instructed on the internships page.

verification.notes: From the IIMCB internships page.

warnings: Only 30 international participants receive the YTB stipend and flight — others must fund themselves.
programmes.title: Sabancı University PURE Summer Research Program (with Türkiye Scholarships)
programmes.summary: A seven-week summer research programme in Istanbul for undergraduates of any department, with free campus accommodation; 30 international participants also receive a Türkiye Scholarships (YTB) stipend and flights.
programmes.fields: All departments (projects listed by Sabancı faculty)
eligibility: Undergraduate students of any year and department (graduate students are not eligible).
Good academic standing and enough English for the project (no English test required).
Must not be doing another internship at the same time; must live on campus for the full 7 weeks.
programmes.nationalities: Domestic and international undergraduates.
programmes.stipend: Free shared dormitory for all accepted students. 30 international students selected by YTB also get a monthly stipend (13,000 TL in 2026) and a round-trip flight; others pay their own travel and living costs.

dates.deadlineNote: The summer 2027 calendar has not been published. In 2026, student applications ran 15–29 April.

procedure: Browse the projects on the PURE website when the summer call opens.
Apply online to up to 6 projects with your transcript and statement of purpose (no fee).
Accepted international students are automatically considered for the YTB scholarship.

verification.notes: From the Sabancı University PURE requirements, calendar and announcement pages.
